issues.description: The template's Farm.java does not provide the expected Farm class and structure described in the problem UML. Instead the file declares a class named AnimalFarm (mismatching the filename Farm.java), contains duplicate/embedded package and class declarations and incomplete/malformed method stubs. The problem statement and solution expect a public class Farm with a List<Animal> animals attribute, addAnimal(Animal), feedAllAnimals(), and singFarmSong() methods; the template lacks the animals list and the correct class name/signature. This mismatch (filename vs. public class name, missing attribute and methods) will prevent students from compiling and implementing the intended design and is therefore a major structural inconsistency.
issues.suggestedFix: Replace the malformed template file with a correctly named public class Farm (matching Farm.java) that declares the animals attribute as List<Animal> and the methods addAnimal(Animal), feedAllAnimals(), and singFarmSong(). Remove duplicate package/class blocks and ensure the class name matches the filename. Also provide or include stubs for the other required types (abstract Animal, interfaces Rideable and Milkable, and concrete classes Pig, Goat, Seal) so students have the correct structural foundation to implement the exercise.

issues.description: The problem statement and solution describe and implement a class named 'Farm', but the template repository provides a class named 'AnimalFarm' in Farm.java. This inconsistent identifier for the same core entity (the farm) will confuse students: they will look for a 'Farm' class (as required and referenced in the Main and problem description) but find 'AnimalFarm', causing mapping and compilation friction.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template class from 'AnimalFarm' to 'Farm' (so the public class matches the problem description and file name). Ensure the class declaration is 'public class Farm' in Farm.java and update any internal references to use 'Farm' to align template, problem statement, and solution.
